title: Grateful Dead Live at Public Hall on 1973-12-06
lineage: CD -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> Samplitude Professional v10.22 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a legendary 12/6/73 Cleveland show – soaring Dark Star and an unforgettable Here Comes Sunshine.
ai_review.review: The Miller‑sourced soundboard tape delivers crystal‑clear instrument separation, letting the band’s interplay shine. Musically the concert is highlighted by a colossal, space‑y Dark Star, a transcendent Here Comes Sunshine, and tight China Cat → Rider, with Phil Lesh’s bass and Keith Godchaux’s electric piano stealing much of the spotlight. The first set is solid but not as inspired as the second‑set marathon, making this one of ’73’s most celebrated performances.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 4–5 stars and praise both performance and Miller's soundboard transfer; only a handful of low‑star outliers keep the average just below the top tier.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Miller’s SBD transfer is lauded as crisp, well‑balanced and free of audience patches; reviewers note superb clarity of guitar, bass and Keith's Rhodes, with no audible dropouts.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A solid first set of rockers and cowboy tunes gives way to a second‑set marathon where the Dark Star unfolds into Eyes → Stella Blue, bookended by a fiery Here Comes Sunshine; the pacing is praised for its dynamic highs despite a few reviewers finding the opening set less thrilling.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly highlighted for his soaring, inventive solos—especially on Here Comes Sunshine and throughout Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Phil: Widely praised for thunderous, melodic bass work and experimental “Seastones” textures that drive the jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for a clean rhythm‑guitar tone and solid vocal contributions in several reviews.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux’s electric piano is singled out as jazzy, inventive and a key driver of the night’s atmosphere.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann described as “on fire,” providing steady propulsion behind the extended improvisations.
